answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a scarce resource nobody rents cheaply: a hardware-bound seat. Each agent must forge its keypair inside a secure enclave that signs a per-epoch liveness challenge, and that seat is bonded, slashed the moment two enclaves report identical entropy. A farmer cannot spawn ten thousand puppets from one island of shared silicon; he must buy ten thousand distinct chips. The marginal cost of the next fake identity climbs a steep, rising ledge of hardware spend plus slashing risk, so a swarm stops paying once the bond exceeds the per-seat emission.
